The attacker's own connection configuration was persisted but unused for as long as the colliding cache entry survived.

### Impact

A base Creator with no role on the victim base could reflect the victim's external database schema into their own base and then read, update and insert records in that database through their own models - crossing the base boundary into a database owned by a different tenant, with writes confirmed visible to the victim through their original model. Direct requests against the victim base's metadata and records were refused throughout. Exploitation requires an authenticated account with the Creator role on one unrelated base, knowledge of the victim source id (shared-view metadata exposes it), and the victim connection to be cached in the process handling the request.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@bwbugs](https://github.com/bwbugs).

advisories.title: Row Filter Bypass via Shared View Relation Endpoints
advisories.summary:
### Summary

The public shared-view relation endpoints confirmed that the parent record named in the URL existed in the table, but not that it survived the view's row filters, so an anonymous caller could read relation data hanging off records the shared view was configured to hide.

### Details

The relation handlers in `public-datas.service.ts` resolved the parent record with a plain primary-key read in `BaseModelSqlv2.ts`. That read applied the model's primary-key lookup and the usual soft-delete handling, but not the view's root filter list, unlike the list and count paths on the same share, which do apply it. The has-many, many-to-many, link, and one-many routes registered in `public-datas.controller.ts` all reached that same check, so any record id in the underlying table could be supplied as the parent of a relation read regardless of whether the view's filters excluded it. The retry path used for formula columns carried the same weakness, so it could not fail closed either.

### Impact

An attacker holding only the public share link could substitute the id of a filtered-out record - trivially guessable, since record ids default to an auto-incrementing integer - and retrieve the child records linked to it, defeating the row filters that define what a shared view is allowed to publish. No authentication is required.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@XlabAITeam](https://github.com/XlabAITeam), [@keenanwgn](https://github.com/keenanwgn), [@liangjs](https://github.com/liangjs) and [@A7um](https://github.com/A7um).

advisories.title: NocoDB from 0.300.0 before 2026.04.4 Denial of Service via MetaService Logging
advisories.summary: NocoDB from 0.300.0 before 2026.04.4 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to crash the server by triggering an unhandled promise rejection in MetaService metadata logging. Attackers can send a request leaving a lookup condition undefined, causing knex binding errors in the unawaited logHelper call that terminate the server process.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 Attachment Size Limit Bypass via Upload by URL
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains an attachment size limit bypass that allows authenticated Editor users to store oversized files because data-attachment-v3.service.ts trusts the remote server's advertised content length. Attackers can point the v3 upload-by-URL endpoint at a server that understates or omits its length to exhaust disk space or storage quota.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.06.1 CSV Formula Injection via export.service.ts
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.06.1 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability in export.service.ts that writes record values and column titles beginning with formula characters into CSV exports without neutralization. Low-privileged collaborators, or unauthenticated users submitting a public form, can plant formulas that execute when a user opens the export in a spreadsheet application, potentially exfiltrating cell contents or invoking external commands.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Reflected XSS via ncRedirectUrl in PageLeavingWarning.vue
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in PageLeavingWarning.vue that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute script by embedding an ASCII control character in the ncRedirectUrl scheme. Attackers can send a crafted link that bypasses the scheme check and reaches the anchor href or window.location, stealing the session token from localStorage for account takeover.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 Stored XSS via AI Field Prompt Tooltip
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in PromptWithFields.vue that renders unescaped field references from AI field prompts as HTML in a tooltip. Attackers with the Creator role or above can store markup in a prompt's field reference that executes when victims open the field configuration, stealing the localStorage session token to call authenticated APIs as the victim.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Stored XSS via Table Deletion Dialog
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator users to inject script by embedding markup in column or table titles. The Delete.vue confirmation dialog renders these titles through an unescaped innerHTML binding, executing script when a victim deletes an external-source table to steal session tokens from localStorage.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 Stored XSS via Attachment MIME Type
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Editor users to execute scripts by storing crafted attachment MIME types like text/html;image/png. Attackers can write the value through the records API so the /dltemp signed URL serves HTML inline, stealing session tokens from localStorage to impersonate victims.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 SQL Injection via User Email in Base User Query
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in base-user.cte.utils.ts, which concatenates base members' email addresses into the SQL text of queries resolving user, created-by or last-modified-by fields. Registered users can set an email with a quoted local part containing a single quote to execute arbitrary SQL, exposing user records, API tokens and data-source credentials.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 SQL Injection via Legacy where Query Filter
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with read access to run arbitrary read queries via the legacy where parameter on PostgreSQL. Attackers, including Viewer-role users, can inject single quotes into filter values concatenated by CustomKnex.ts to read other tables, schemas, view-filtered rows, and hidden columns.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 TLS Private Key Exposure via Data Source Read
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated base Viewers to obtain TLS client private keys by reading a base's data source. The source read handler masked only the connection password, letting attackers retrieve the decrypted private key, client certificate and CA to connect directly to the external database, bypassing NocoDB permissions.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.07.0 Private Integration Credential Exposure via Base Integration Read
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in base-integrations.service.ts that allows authenticated base members to read private integration configurations by omitting a query flag. Attackers can request another user's private integration without the configuration flag, bypassing the ownership check to obtain stored connection credentials.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Private Integration Credential Exposure via Copy
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the copy-from branch of integration creation in integrations.service.ts that decrypts a source integration's connection credentials without checking its owner or private flag. Authenticated users with the Creator role can supply guessed or enumerated integration ids to copy other users' private database host, username, and password into an integration they own.

advisories.title: NocoDB 2026.05.2 before 2026.07.0 SSRF via Data Import URL Fetch
advisories.summary: NocoDB from 2026.05.2 before 2026.07.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Editor-role users to fetch internal URLs because data import reused the webhook internal-network exemption. When NC_ALLOW_LOCAL_HOOKS or NC_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK is set, attackers can request internal services via URLs ending in CSV or spreadsheet extensions and read the responses.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 IP Address Spoofing via Unconditional Proxy Trust
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an IP address spoofing vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge their recorded source IP by supplying X-Forwarded-For headers, because Express trust proxy is enabled unconditionally. Attackers can write arbitrary source addresses into audit and request logs to mislead investigations and evade the per-address public API rate limiter.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.06.1 Password Hash Exposure via Profile Update Response
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.06.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the profile update handler in users.service.ts, which returns the stored user record without passing it through the user-serialization filter, exposing the bcrypt password hash, salt, and session token counter. Attackers holding a stolen or hijacked session can update the profile to retrieve that account's password hash and salt for offline cracking.

advisories.title: NocoDB from 2026.04.0 before 2026.08.0 Improper Privilege Management via Organization Role Update
advisories.summary: NocoDB from 2026.04.0 before 2026.08.0 contains an improper privilege management vulnerability in org-users.service.ts where updating a user's legacy organization role rewrites their default-workspace role. Revoked users can silently regain Creator-level read, write and schema modification access across all default-workspace bases using their existing session token.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 Privilege Escalation via Incomplete Admin Bootstrap
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in initAdminFromEnv.ts that silently skips super-admin bootstrap when the admin password environment variable is empty. Unauthenticated attackers can call the public signup endpoint first on a fresh instance to receive Creator and Super Admin roles, gaining full administrative control.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 Password Reset Token Race Condition
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains a race condition vulnerability in users.service.ts that allows holders of a valid reset token to perform multiple password changes by sending concurrent reset requests. Attackers can exploit the window created by slow bcrypt hashing before the token is cleared to overwrite the owner's new password and lock them out.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 Credential Disclosure via Public OAuth Client Endpoint
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve full OAuth client records by querying the public client lookup route in oauth.controller.ts. Attackers who know or guess a client identifier can obtain the registration access token to modify or delete registrations, plus the bcrypt client secret hash and owner's internal identifier.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 Client Authentication Bypass via OAuth Token Exchange
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in oauth-token.service.ts that treats PKCE as a substitute for confidential client authentication, skipping client secret verification when omitted. Attackers holding a captured authorization code and PKCE verifier can mint access tokens and 60-day refresh tokens for a confidential client without knowing its secret.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.09.1 Unauthenticated Information Disclosure via Aggregated Meta Endpoint
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the aggregated meta info route of utils.controller.ts that exposes instance-wide metadata to anonymous callers. Unauthenticated attackers can request the endpoint to enumerate bases, user counts, shared and password-protected view counts, webhook counts, and live per-base row counts, while repeated requests amplify database query load.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 IDOR in Row Comment Operations
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read cross-base row comments by supplying only model and row ids. Attackers with a Viewer or Creator role on an unrelated base can read private comments and author emails, or plant decoy tables and duplicate comment ids to spoof teammates' comments.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Incorrect Authorization via Base-Scoped API Tokens
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that lets base-scoped API tokens act as account-wide credentials because the token's base_id is never stored or checked. Attackers holding a leaked token can read, write and delete records on every base the token owner belongs to, including bases joined later.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption via Bulk Record Endpoints
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass bulk row-count limits by using session authentication instead of API tokens. Attackers with Editor write permission on one table can submit hundreds of thousands of rows to v1 and v2 bulk write routes, exhausting database connections, CPU, and memory.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption via Shared View Bulk API
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server resources by sending unbounded filter arrays to shared-view bulk endpoints. Attackers with a shared view UUID can POST a large body of minimal filter objects, triggering a full database query per entry, to crash the NocoDB process.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Clickjacking via Missing Frame-Control Headers
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a clickjacking vulnerability that allows any origin to frame the authenticated interface because no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors headers are sent. Attackers can overlay a signed-in user's session from a malicious page, tricking clicks that modify or delete records, change sharing settings, or invite collaborators.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 Refresh Token Reuse via Non-Atomic Rotation
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a race condition in refresh-token rotation that allows attackers to reuse tokens because UserRefreshToken.ts never checks the affected-row count. Attackers holding a captured refresh token can present it concurrently with the legitimate user to obtain a valid authenticated session, and no reuse event is recorded.

advisories.title: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 OAuth Refresh Token Rotation Race Condition
advisories.summary: NocoDB before 2026.06.2 contains a race condition vulnerability in oauth-token.service.ts that allows attackers to reuse a refresh token by presenting it concurrently during non-atomic rotation. Attackers holding a captured refresh token can race the legitimate client to obtain their own access and refresh tokens, retaining scoped access without triggering reuse detection.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Server-Side Request Forgery via Spreadsheet Import Endpoint
advisories.summary:
NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, the spreadsheet-import endpoint axiosRequestMake could be used as a generic HTTP proxy. Before the fix it was reachable unauthenticated, and its URL-extension allowlist was a regex tested against the full URL string, so URLs whose query string ended in .csv satisfies the gate even though the
underlying request is for another file. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Server-Side Request Forgery via Spreadsheet Fetch URL
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, the spreadsheet-fetch endpoint (axiosRequestMake) accepted URLs whose path contained a permitted extension anywhere in the string, and applied a hand-rolled regex blocklist that omitted 127.0.0.0/8 and 169.254.0.0/16, allowing the cloud-metadata endpoint to be reached with a crafted URL This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Server-Side Request Forgery via Base Migration URL
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, the base-migration endpoint accepted a caller-supplied URL that the migration worker dereferenced without enforcing protocol or destination, allowing scheme abuse (file:, ftp:, etc.) and probing of internal HTTP destinations. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Secure Attachment
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, with NC_SECURE_ATTACHMENTS=true, an authenticated uploader could deliver .html or .svg attachments that the browser rendered inline from the NocoDB origin instead of forcing a download. The signed attachment handler stored response-header overrides under PascalCase keys (ResponseContentDisposition, ResponseContentType) while the controller that served the file read them under lowercase-hyphen names (response-content-disposition). The mismatch dropped the Content-Disposition: attachment header, leaving Express to auto-render .html, .svg, and similar inline. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Refresh Tokens Persist Through Password Recovery
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, a stolen refresh token survived a password-forgot flow and could be used to mint fresh JWTs even after the user reset their password. passwordChange and passwordReset deleted the user's refresh tokens, but passwordForgot only rotated token_version and revoked OAuth tokens - it did not call UserRefreshToken.deleteAllUserToken(user.id). An attacker holding a captured refresh cookie could still exchange it for a new access token after the victim triggered the recovery flow. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Hidden LTAR Column Exposure in Public Shared-View Relation Endpoints
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, the public shared-view relation endpoints accepted a caller-supplied column ID without verifying that the column was visible in the shared view, so anyone holding a share UUID could read links from any LTAR column on the view's table - including columns the view owner had hidden. publicMmList, publicHmList, and relDataList already ensured that the requested column belonged to the view's model, but did not check the view-column entry's show flag. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Postgres SQL Injection in Formula `ARRAYSORT`
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, an authenticated user with columnAdd permission on a Postgres-backed base can inject arbitrary SQL into the formula engine via the optional direction argument of ARRAYSORT(...). The value is unrestricted by formula validation and embedded into a knex.raw ORDER BY clause, executing during column creation and on every subsequent record read of the formula column. The vulnerability is specific to the Postgres mapping for ARRAYSORT in packages/nocodb/src/db/functionMappings/pg.ts. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via Password Reset Token
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, the password-reset page rendered the URL token directly into a JavaScript string literal in a server-rendered EJS template. EJS <%= %> HTML-entity-encodes a fixed set of characters but does not escape single quotes or backslashes, so a crafted token could break out of the JS string context and execute attacker-controlled script in the NocoDB origin. Triggering required only that a victim follow a malicious password-reset link. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Open Redirect via Hash Fragment in hashRedirect Plugin
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, the client-side hashRedirect plugin called window.location.replace() on a path extracted from the URL hash fragment after only checking hashPath.startsWith('/'). Protocol-relative URLs (//attacker.com/…) also satisfy that check, so a crafted link silently redirected visitors to an attacker-controlled origin. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Hidden Column Exposure in Public Shared View Endpoints
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, Public shared-view endpoints exposed values from columns that the view owner had hidden, via three independent paths: groupBy returned raw values for any column named in the request, filter and sort arrays operated on hidden columns enabling boolean-blind extraction, and the related-data list accepted arbitrary link-column IDs from other tables in the same base. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Plaintext Password Comparison in Shared Views
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, the shared-view password check fell back to strict-equality (===) comparison for legacy plaintext passwords, leaking the password's length and per-character prefix through response timing. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: User Enumeration via Sign-In Timing
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, sign-in response timing differed between known and unknown email addresses because the unknown-user branch returned without performing a password hash comparison. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Missing Ownership Check in MCP Attachment Read
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, a low-privilege MCP token holder with knowledge of an attachment path could read any file in shared storage, including attachments belonging to other bases and workspaces, because the MCP readAttachment tool did not verify the file's ownership. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Server-Side Request Forgery via Database Connection Host
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, the connection-test endpoint opened a raw TCP socket to the user-supplied database host without resolving and range-checking the destination, so private and link-local addresses (including IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms and localhost) reached the driver. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Cross-Workspace Integration Use in Connection Test
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, a user in one workspace could exercise another workspace's integration through the testConnection endpoint by supplying its ID, because the integration was fetched in a bypass scope and the caller's permission check matched any base in any workspace. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: OAuth Tokens Persist Through Security Events
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, revokeAllOAuthTokensByUser in the users service is an empty stub being called from passwordChange, passwordForgot, and passwordReset. OAuth access and refresh tokens were not revoked when the user changed, reset, or recovered their password, leaving an attacker-issued OAuth grant valid after the user believed they had locked the attacker out. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Row Comments
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, an authenticated commenter could store HTML in row comments that executed as script when other users hovered over the comment in the expanded form view. The comment write paths persisted the raw comment body with no server-side sanitisation; the expanded-form sidebar then rendered the stored body and fed its data-tooltip attribute to Tippy with allowHTML: true. Even when the editor stripped script tags at write time, attribute-level payloads re-entered the DOM as live HTML on hover. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Path Traversal via SQLite Source Filename
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, an authenticated user with base-create permission can attach a SQLite source pointing at an arbitrary file on the NocoDB host, including NocoDB's own internal databases. The SQLite client and the base/integration create services accepted a caller-supplied filename and passed it to fs.exists and fs.open('w') without restricting the location. A user could point a source at noco.db, at a tenant database under nc_minimal_dbs/, or at any writable path the NocoDB process can reach, and then read or overwrite its contents through the regular table APIs.This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: SQL Injection via Column Title in Bulk GroupBy
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, an authenticated user with column-create permission can inject SQL into the bulk groupBy endpoint by setting a column's title to a SQL fragment. The bulk groupBy path in group-by.ts builds three database-specific knex.raw() aggregations that interpolate the request's column_name directly into the SQL string. Column lookup in data-table.service.ts matches on both the sanitized column_name field and the free-text title, so a title containing a SQL fragment bypasses the public endpoint's existing column allowlist and reaches the query builder unescaped. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: OAuth Authorization Code Race Condition
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, two concurrent token-exchange requests using the same OAuth authorization code could each mint a distinct valid (access_token, refresh_token) pair, breaking the single-use guarantee that PKCE relies on. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Form View Redirect URL
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.05.1, the shared form-view submit handler (packages/nc-gui/composables/useSharedFormViewStore.ts) in NocoDB writes the form's redirect_url to window.location.href after a same-host check that does not validate the URL scheme. A user with editor role (or above) on any base can plant a javascript: URL in the form's redirect_url; when an authenticated viewer opens the share-link and submits the form, the payload executes in the NocoDB origin and can read the session token from localStorage["nocodb-gui-v2"]. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.05.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Attachment Size Limit Bypass via Upload-by-URL
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, the upload-by-URL path did not enforce NC_ATTACHMENT_FIELD_SIZE against either the remote file's advertised Content-Length or the decoded length of a data: URI, allowing an authenticated user to bypass the configured per-file size limit. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stale Auth Cache After API Token Deletion
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.4, deleted API tokens continued to authenticate requests until their cache entry expired, because the auth cache was not invalidated by token value at deletion time. The API token deletion path removed the database row but did not evict the token-value keyed entry from the auth cache. The auth middleware therefore continued to accept the deleted token until the cache entry aged out, leaving a deletion-to-revocation window of up to three days. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.4.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Shared-base link access can invite arbitrary users as persistent base members
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, shared-base sessions were granted the same base-member capabilities as authenticated viewers. Using only the shared-base UUID (xc-shared-base-id), an attacker could enumerate base members and invite an arbitrary email into the base as a real member. The invited user could then redeem the invite via the normal signup flow and retain authenticated access even after the owner revoked the shared link. Shared-base sessions were mapped to ProjectRoles.VIEWER in packages/nocodb/src/strategies/base-view.strategy/base-view.strategy.ts, and packages/nocodb/src/utils/acl.ts granted baseUserList and userInvite to that role. The shared frontend (packages/nc-gui/composables/useApi/interceptors.ts) deliberately removed auth headers in favour of the shared-base header, but the ACL middleware did not distinguish shared sessions from genuine viewers. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Refresh Token Cookie Set Without `Secure` and `SameSite` Flags
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, the refresh-token cookie was set with httpOnly: true but missing both the secure flag and the sameSite attribute. Over plain HTTP the cookie could be intercepted on the network; without sameSite, browsers attached it to cross-site POSTs, enabling CSRF against the token-refresh endpoint. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Missing File Size Enforcement in Upload-by-URL Allows Denial of Service via Disk Exhaustion
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.4, the uploadViaURL path in the v1/v2 attachment API did not enforce NC_ATTACHMENT_FIELD_SIZE against the remote content-length or against the response stream. An authenticated user (Editor+) could direct the server to download arbitrarily large files, exhausting disk space and causing denial of service. In packages/nocodb/src/services/attachments.service.ts, the HEAD probe read content-length but never compared it to NC_ATTACHMENT_FIELD_SIZE; the subsequent storageAdapter.fileCreateByUrl() performed the download without maxContentLength. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.4.

advisories.title: NocoDB: OAuth Token Scope Not Enforced at ACL Layer Allows Scope Escalation
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, the OAuth token strategy attached oauth_scope and oauth_granted_resources to the request user, but the ACL middleware never consulted either. An OAuth token issued with a restricted scope (e.g. MCP-only) therefore inherited the full permissions of the underlying user across all routes; the granted_resources.base_id restriction was bypassed on org-level endpoints that don't populate req.context.base_id. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: SSRF Protection Bypass in Notification Webhook Plugins (Slack, Discord, Mattermost, Teams)
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, the request-filtering-agent SSRF protection was non-functional in the four notification webhook plugins (Slack, Discord, Mattermost, Teams) because httpAgent / httpsAgent were passed as part of the request body rather than the axios config. An authenticated user with hook-creation permission could direct outbound POST requests to arbitrary internal hosts. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via Page Leaving Redirect URL
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.04.1, a reflected XSS vulnerability exists in the Page Leaving Warning page. The ncRedirectUrl and ncBackUrl query parameters are used in window.location.href and <a> tag bindings without validation, allowing javascript: URI injection. This vulnerability is fixed in 2026.04.1.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Rich Text Cells
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, rich text cell content rendered via v-html without sanitization enables stored XSS. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comments
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, comments rendered via v-html without sanitization enable stored XSS. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: SQL Injection via DATEADD Formula
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, an authenticated user with Creator role can inject arbitrary SQL via the DATEADD formula's unit parameter. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comments and Rich Text Cells
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, user-controlled content in comments and rich text cells was rendered via v-html without sanitization, enabling stored XSS. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Refresh Tokens Not Revoked on Password Reset
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, the password reset flow did not revoke existing refresh tokens, allowing an attacker with a previously stolen refresh token to continue minting valid JWTs after the victim resets their password. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Missing Ownership Validation in MCP Token Operations
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, the MCP token service did not validate token ownership, allowing a Creator within the same base to read, regenerate, or delete another user's MCP tokens if the token ID was known. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Plaintext Storage of Shared View Passwords
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, shared view passwords were stored in plaintext in the database and compared using direct string equality. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: User Enumeration via Password Reset Endpoint
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, the password forgot endpoint returned different responses for registered and unregistered emails, allowing user enumeration. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Rich Text Field
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, an authenticated user with Editor role can inject arbitrary HTML into Rich Text cells by bypassing the TipTap editor and sending raw HTML via the API. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Formula Cell
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.3, a stored XSS vulnerability exists in the Formula virtual cell. Formula results containing URI::() patterns are rendered via v-html without sanitization, allowing injected HTML to execute. This issue has been patched in version 0.301.3.

advisories.title: NocoDB Vulnerable to Prototype Pollution in Connection Test Endpoint, Leading to DoS
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.0, an authenticated user with org-level-creator permissions can exploit prototype pollution in the `/api/v2/meta/connection/test` endpoint, causing all database write operations to fail application-wide until server restart. While the pollution technically bypasses SUPER_ADMIN authorization checks, no practical privileged actions can be performed because database operations fail immediately after pollution. Version 0.301.0 patches the issue.

advisories.title: NocoDB has Blind SSRF via Unvalidated HEAD Request in uploadViaURL Functionality
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.0, a blind Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in the `uploadViaURL` functionality due to an unprotected `HEAD` request. While the subsequent file retrieval logic correctly enforces SSRF protections, the initial metadata request executes without validation. This allows limited outbound requests to arbitrary URLs before SSRF controls are applied. Version 0.301.0 contains a patch for the issue.

advisories.title: NocoDB Vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via SVG upload
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.0, a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in NocoDB’s attachment handling mechanism. Authenticated users can upload malicious SVG files containing embedded JavaScript, which are later rendered inline and executed in the browsers of other users who view the attachment. Because the malicious payload is stored server-side and executed under the application’s origin, successful exploitation can lead to account compromise, data exfiltration and unauthorized actions performed on behalf of affected users. Version 0.301.0 patches the issue.

advisories.title: NocoDB has Unvalidated Redirect in Login Flow via continueAfterSignIn Parameter
advisories.summary: NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to version 0.301.0, an unvalidated redirect (open redirect) vulnerability exists in NocoDB’s login flow due to missing validation of the `continueAfterSignIn` parameter. During authentication, NocoDB processes a user-controlled redirect value and conditionally performs client-side navigation without enforcing any restrictions on the destination’s origin, domain or protocol. This allows attackers to redirect authenticated users to arbitrary external websites after login. This vulnerability enables phishing attacks by leveraging user trust in the legitimate NocoDB login flow. While it does not directly expose credentials or bypass authentication, it increases the likelihood of credential theft through social engineering. The issue does not allow arbitrary code execution or privilege escalation, but it undermines authentication integrity. Version 0.301.0 fixes the issue.
